newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Eight killed in latest Colombian rebel violence.
newsitem.headline: Eight killed in latest Colombian rebel violence.

text.p: Eight people died in the latest round of fighting across Colombia, including two policemen killed in a leftist rebel attack near one of the country's prime oil fields, officials said on Monday.
They said the dead included four guerrillas and a soldier killed in firefights on Sunday in the country's north and a mayor gunned down in southeast Caqueta province.
National Liberation Army (ELN) rebels killed the two policemen in the town of Aguazul, in Casanare province, about 100 miles (160 km) northeast of the capital Bogota, police sources said.
Operations in the nearby Cusiana oil field operated by British Petroleum were not affected, a spokesman said.
The ELN, Colombia's second-largest guerrilla force, specializes in attacks on the nation's oil infrastructure and against multinational companies.

The weekend clashes come against the backdrop of the bloodiest guerrilla offensive in decades, unleashed with an attack on a military base in southern Putumayo province, in which 27 soldiers died, on Aug. 30.
At least 60 soldiers were taken prisoner by the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) in that raid. Efforts are continuing to secure their release.

In a communique on Monday, the FARC, the country's largest guerrilla force, warned that military operations in southern jungle regions were putting the lives of their captives at risk. It called on the International Committee of the Red Cross to carry out checks in Caqueta if the army failed to demilitarize part of the province within 10 days -- one of the rebels' conditions for handing over the troops.

Over the weekend former senator Alvaro Leyva, a member of the commission due to witness the release of the prisoners, said the handover was being delayed by the government's failure to name its own representative to the delegation.

Colombia's anti-kidnap chief Alberto Villamizar was expected to take on the role. He said on Monday he would be prepared to head the official mediation effort for the troops but said he had not yet been invited.
